notes.text: This is a continuation leaf beginning “qui forment un groupoïde”. It defines finite graph data (S, vector A, sigma, o), permits isolated vertices, loops, multiple edges and free edges, and adds supplementary structure.

The first displayed map assigns a genre or poids to vertices. The second is captioned indice de rigidification. The live 2 beside its crossed former label is preserved on the baseline; no mathematical interpretation is used to delete it or force it into a subscript.

The crossed lower inclusion and the crossed proposal using S-tilde are retained as cancelled work. The pondération du graphe caption is outside the enclosure and remains live because no cancellation crosses it.

The diagonal margin note says that the data are not precise enough and that an edge weighting should be replaced by a combinatorial pol. T_a with the stated omega relation. The page does not establish the meaning of pol. or prove that relation; its second T subscript remains open.

The enclosed note says that vertex weights have been indicated but edge weights have not. The adjacent drawing contains seven connected weighted vertices and an isolated vertex labelled 2, followed below by a three-arm vertex 0 and a loop at vertex 3. Pale centers, gaps and thin arms are retained as drawing features.

The marginal decomposition separates nonfixed and fixed elements of the involution and labels their quotient maps degree 2 and degree 1. The lower paragraph states that an ordinary graph together with a finite free-edge set and its attachment to S recovers the graph with free edges. Check B047-K01 verifies these claims conditionally on the stated definitions.

Sigma is used both for the involution on vector A and in the local order notation sigma(s)=sigma_ell(s)+sigma_0(s). The latter ell component is associated on the page with holes or gluing circles. This notational reuse is retained.
The top 3) is the manuscript’s own page number. The bottom 46 is written in a separate thin hand and is retained as an unassigned margin foliation; no attribution is inferred.

H’s explanatory notes and repeated align formulas are editorial witnesses, not extra source text. The source has one decomposition diagram with explanatory formulas under brackets. C’s extra A_ell before the crossed arêtes-libres gloss has no independently visible token and is omitted.

The first involution-map shaft has only a small terminal tip; no hook or origin bar has been added. The final attachment-map A is retraced, but no independent earlier letter is secure. A faint isolated spot below its S is not treated as punctuation.

checks.outcome: Verified conditionally on sigma being an involution and o: vector A -> S being the stated origin map. If a is not fixed, sigma(a) differs from a and sigma(sigma(a))=a, so its orbit has exactly two elements. A fixed element has a one-element orbit. Thus the quotient restricts to degree 2 on vector A minus vector A^sigma and degree 1 on vector A^sigma, as labelled. Restricting o and sigma to the nonfixed part gives the ordinary graph; retaining the fixed elements as A_ell with their o-values gives A_ell -> S. Conversely adjoining those fixed elements with this attachment reconstructs the original unweighted graph data. This check does not decide the cancelled domain exponent, the live 2 beside r, or the marginal T subscript.
